#6222. 25 Best Credit Card Offers & Bonuses For Travel Rewards In November 2026

For those with access to credit cards in the United States, the single best way to rack up a lot of points quickly is by taking advantage of the best credit card welcome bonuses and offers. The credit card industry in the United States is lucrative (for banks, airlines, hotel groups, etc.), and the idea is that they often offer large upfront welcome offers and bonuses to incentivize people to apply.

So in this post, I’d like to share what I consider to be the best current credit card welcome bonuses and offers for earning travel rewards, across a variety of categories. The details of the best offers are always changing, so that’s why I think it’s useful to keep a current list with the best credit card welcome bonuses, which I try to constantly update to reflect offers.

I’ll share what I consider the 25 best credit card welcome offers right now to be, across five categories (business transferable points cards, personal transferable points cards, hotel cards, airline cards, and no annual fee cards). Before I do, let me just point out a few things:

Simply put, most people want to travel better, but don’t know how. One of the best ways to improve your travel experience is to pick up an excellent credit card that can add value to your wallet.

When applying for a credit card, consider three main points:

In this post I’m focusing primarily on the best credit card welcome bonuses, which can be one of the best ways to get rewarded quickly. Often a good credit card bonus will be enough to earn you an international ticket in first or business class, which many would otherwise assume is off limits.

Business credit cards tend to have among the most lucrative welcome offers of any cards out there, so if you’re eligible to apply for them, there are some incredible opportunities. Admittedly these cards often have large minimum spending requirements, but if you can unlock them, these cards can earn you an incredible amount of travel.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on business cards that earn travel rewards. Specifically, these are focused on transferable points currencies, which give you the most flexibility (I’ll cover some airline and hotel business cards below, in separate sections).

Personal credit cards are of course the most popular for those looking to earn travel rewards for their credit card spending. These cards can be all over the place in terms of their annual fees and perks, but many are worth having.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on personal cards that earn travel rewards. Specifically, these are focused on transferable points currencies, which give you the most flexibility (I’ll cover some airline and hotel personal cards below, in separate sections).

I’m a huge fan of hotel credit cards, given the incredible value they can offer on an ongoing basis. Even if you don’t spend a lot on these cards, there’s potentially value to having them, thanks to their perks, like hotel elite status, free night awards, and more.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on hotel credit cards, including both personal and business cards.

There’s lots of merit to getting airline credit cards, given that they can offer priority perks and fee waivers for travel on airlines, and can also help you earn elite status.

Below are what I consider to be the five best welcome offers on airline credit cards, including both personal and business cards.

Admittedly the best credit card welcome offers are typically going to be on credit cards with annual fees. Before applying for the best credit card welcome bonuses, makes sure you’re aware of the rules each bank has for credit card applications. One of the common misconceptions people have is that they think applying for credit cards will hurt their credit. The opposite is largely true, actually. Assuming you use your credit responsibly (and make payments on time, don’t utilize too much of your credit, etc.), applying for credit cards can actually help your credit.

However, if you are going to apply for credit cards, make sure you do so responsibly — only apply for them if you have self-control and won’t end up in debt, and try to pay your balance in full every month, or else the interest charges will negate any rewards earned.

A mother and her 7-year-old son waiting for a flight at the Fort Lauderdale airport were splashed with urine when a man seated across from them exposed himself and began urinating in their direction on Tuesday morning, November 3. Deputies arrested the 48-year old local man on six charges. The arrest affidavit says this happened at gate E6, which tells me this is either an American Airlines or JetBlue passenger. The family said the man was facing them when he unbuttoned his pants and let loose. The father avoided the blast. “Several other passengers were present in the immediate area at the time of the incident,” Powell wrote. “As Raben exposed himself and began urinating, the surrounding passengers dispersed from the area.” The charges were: Battery involving an adult causing a child to come into contact with bodily fluids. Battery. Three counts of indecent exposure. Disorderly intoxication. Go figure: Florida has an actual felony specifically covering an adult knowingly causing, or attempting to cause, a child to come into contact with urine or certain other bodily substances by projecting or expelling them. They knew they needed this. It’s a third-degree felony, punishable by up to five years in prison. He was released on $5,000 bond. Airport surveillance footage of the incident has not been released. Local 10 News reporting on the Fort Lauderdale airport arrest “Urine trouble now, buddy,” one Reddit commenter offered. This happens more than you’d expect (or at least, more than anyone would hope). At Memphis airport a man urinated over a woman sleeping in the terminal. Earlier this year, an Air Canada passenger was filmed urinating on the floor at a Calgary gate while bystanders wondered whether he was sleepwalking. And once you’re on board, getting away becomes harder. A Frontier Airlines passenger who said urine ran onto his leg and shoes was offered a $75 voucher. #6220. Washington Dulles Concourse E Opens, With Huge New United Club

United Airlines is on quite the roll when it comes to opening new concourses and lounges at its hubs. Just recently, I covered how a new United Club opened in Houston (IAH) Terminal B North. This is not only the biggest United Club in the world, but it’s the biggest airport lounge in all of the Americas.

There’s now another update, as we’re seeing the opening of a new United Club at Washington Dulles (IAD) Concourse E. This is the second biggest United Club in the entire system, and it’s also part of a long overdue new concourse for the airport. Let’s first talk about the new lounge, and then about the new concourse.

A brand new United Club is opening in Concourse E at Washington Dulles Airport. The new lounge is nearly 40,000 square feet, with seating for more than 600 customers, making it the carrier’s second largest United Club in the system. Crucially, this also increases United’s club and lounge space at the airport by nearly 70%.

The new lounge has a bar, two buffet stations, eight private phone rooms, complimentary Wi-Fi, and power access at nearly every seat. Unfortunately there are no showers or barista coffee.

As the design is described, it “reflects the character of the Washington, D.C. region through design elements inspired by the historic natural and built environment of the nation’s capital, like the iconic main Dulles terminal architecture, cherry blossoms and the Blue Ridge Mountains.”

The club is located across from gates E14 and E16, and it’s open daily from 5:30AM until 10PM, with an opening on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The lounge follows the standard United Club access policies.

The opening of the new United Club is part of the larger opening of the new Concourse E at Washington Dulles. This is the first new concourse to open at the airport in two decades.

The new concourse is 435,000 square feet, and it has 14 new gates that will exclusively be used by United. United claims that these new gates will increase connectivity by nearly 30% during peak times. The concourse also has direct AeroTrain access, expansive new dining and retail options, and more.

It’s important to keep in mind what a mess United’s current facility at Washington Dulles is, which is what makes this all the more exciting. United primarily operates out of Concourses C and D, which were built as temporary facilities in 1985. 40+ years later, they’re still there. So this new concourse will be a massive boost to the United passenger experience.

We know that Dulles Airport is supposed to undergo a major modernization, which was unveiled by the Trump administration. However, the cost is astronomical (even by the typically inflated airport standards), and things are already well behind schedule.

As you’d expect, this press release has endless quotes from airline, airport, and Trump administration officials. There’s also a fair bit of spin here, like this, from Deputy Secretary of Transportation, Steven Bradbury:

“Under President Trump, America is building again. So far, the construction of United’s new Concourse E has supported 2,700 good paying jobs and brought $1.3 billion in local economic activity to the national capital region. USDOT’s broader partnership with MWAA and United on the Dulles Airport transformation is just beginning, with many more milestones on the horizon. The ultimate winner will be the American people who will enjoy a stunning new gateway to America’s capital for generations to come. Congratulations to MWAA and United for today’s grand unveiling, and we look forward to even greater results in the near future.”

Keep in mind that the “building” of this concourse started under the Biden administration, and not under the Trump administration.

Washington Dulles Airport’s new Concourse E opens to the public on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The new concourse adds 14 gates for United, and most importantly, it looks like a real terminal, and not like a temporary facility. The concourse has a new United Club, which not only looks much improved, but also massively increases lounge capacity.

What do you make of Washington Dulles Airport’s new Concourse, and the new United Club?

#6219. Lufthansa Suddenly Cancels This 13-Hour Nonstop Route: See Map Now

Last month, Lufthansa announced its most extensive route expansion since 2020. For summer 2027, the Star Alliance member is adding ten new long-haul routes across Asia and the Americas, as well as increasing frequencies on several existing services.

While not part of the announcement, the German flag carrier was also scheduled to resume nonstop flights between Munich Airport (MUC) and Hong Kong International Airport (HKG) after several years of absence. However, in its latest weekend schedule update, the airline removed the route altogether.

Lufthansa has been connecting Germany and Hong Kong since 1961, initially operating flights from Frankfurt Airport (FRA). In the 2000s, the airline also introduced flights from Munich. The route continued operating until early 2020 and has remained suspended since then. The German flag carrier was scheduled to resume flights between Munich and Hong Kong on March 28, 2027, using the Airbus A350-900.

This was also the aircraft type used on the route before its suspension in 2020. In fact, over the years, the airline has operated multiple widebody aircraft on the route, including the Airbus A340-300 and A340-600. It also deployed its Airbus A380 superjumbo in 2018 and 2019.

Why Lufthansa has decided not to reinstate the Munich–Hong Kong route remains unknown. Nevertheless, Cathay Pacific, which is Hong Kong's largest airline, will continue to connect the two cities. The airline launched four weekly flights between Munich and Hong Kong in June last year, operating on Mondays, Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, using its A350-900 aircraft.

Lufthansa, meanwhile, will continue to serve Hong Kong from its Frankfurt hub, using the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner. According to schedule data from aviation analytics provider Cirium, the airline is scheduled to operate one daily round-trip flight on the route throughout the year. Cathay Pacific also offers daily flights between Frankfurt and Hong Kong.

This means there will be a total of 18 weekly services from Germany to Hong Kong next summer. Looking more broadly, the German airline is scheduled to operate 76 weekly flights across 11 East Asian routes in summer 2027. These include the return of services to Nagoya and Tokyo Narita in Japan, both from its Frankfurt hub.

From March 29, 2027, the Star Alliance member will operate three weekly flights to Chubu Centrair International Airport (NGO), which it last served in 2020. A day earlier, on March 28, it will also resume daily flights to Tokyo Narita Airport (NRT). The airline last operated passenger flights to Narita in 2017, when it consolidated its Tokyo operations at Haneda Airport (HND).

In general, Lufthansa has been expanding its network from both Frankfurt and Munich. The airline introduced several new destinations this winter and has more routes planned for summer 2027. From its Southern hub, it will launch three weekly flights to Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX) on August 3, operating on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays with the A350-900. It will also increase frequencies to Bangalore, Chicago, São Paulo and Singapore.

It would not be surprising to see the German flag carrier adding more routes from Munich in the future, especially given its plans to expand its long-haul operations at the airport. It has extended its joint venture agreement with Munich Airport until 2056. Under the agreement, both parties plan to expand terminal infrastructure and support the growth of Lufthansa's long-haul fleet and operations at the airport.

Munich is already home to the airline's A380 fleet and remains its main hub for the A350-900. According to Cirium schedule data, the airline has scheduled about 6,341 flights using the A350-900 from Munich between January and October 2027, compared to 1,492 from Frankfurt. This is an increase of 7% at Munich and 70% at Frankfurt compared to the same period in 2026.

#6218. Brit Jailed In Singapore After Hidden Camera Found In Airplane Lavatory

A man is facing quite some legal challenges after installing a hidden camera in an airplane lavatory, and then trying to control it remotely. Of course this is not only incredibly creepy and illegal, but if you’re going to do something like this, it probably shouldn’t be on a Singapore-bound flight, given the country’s strict laws.

The Straits Times has the story of how a 52-year-old British man has been jailed in Singapore, following an incident that happened on an October 7 flight from Osaka Kansai (KIX) to Singapore Changi (SIN). The man was traveling on a Boeing 787 belonging to Scoot, Singapore Airlines’ low cost subsidiary.

A short time after takeoff, the man reportedly installed a camera in the airplane lavatory, which had the function to be controlled remotely through an app on his phone. A short while later, a flight attendant, who was using the lavatory, found the hidden camera. She removed the device, and of course alerted the crew.

The passenger reportedly tried to remove the camera from the lavatory later, only to find that it was no longer there. The crew managed to figure out who it belonged to (it’s not entirely clear how), though in the meantime, he had already deleted the app on his phone, and all related pictures, to avoid detection.

He was detained upon arrival in Singapore, and his camera and phone were seized. The man was jailed, and his trial will take place in the coming weeks.

He faces charges of voyeurism and obstructing the course of justice. For voyeurism, one can be jailed for up to two years, fined, caned, or a combination of these punishments. For obstructing the course of justice, one can be jailed for up to seven years, fined, or both.

I’m not here to kink shame. People can conceptually be into whatever they want, as far as I’m concerned. The issue is when they non-consensually involve others in whatever that fantasy may be, especially when it violates the law (obviously). A few thoughts come to mind:

While not exactly the same thing, keep in mind that phones sold in South Korea have to make a sound when pictures or videos are taken, even if a phone is set to silent. That’s intended to combat illicit and covert photography of people, against their will. So obviously being creepy in this way is something that’s way more common than it should be…

A British national is facing some serious punishment in Singapore, after he installed hidden cameras in a lavatory of a Scoot Boeing 787. A flight attendant noticed these while using the lavatory, and removed the camera. He later came back to try to retrieve it, and was caught.

The man is now facing charges of voyeurism and obstructing the course of justice, and could be looking at years in jail.

What do you make of this Scoot hidden camera incident?

#6217. Marriott Becomes Giant Anti-ICE Billboard As L.A. Protesters Project ‘Blood Money’ Onto Its Walls

Protesters turned a the Warner Center Marriott Woodland Hills into a giant anti-ICE billboard Sunday night, projecting “Marriott takes blood money from ICE” onto its exterior while the hotel’s own logo remained lit up beside it. Spotted at Woodland Hills Marriott where ICE is reportedly staying. — Raider (@iwillnotbesilenced.bsky.social) November 9, 2026 The messages include “Marriott houses the Gestapo,” “Marriott loves Trump” (with a heart), and “Marriott devours your tax dollars for fascism.” The closing message is: “We beat you before. We will beat you again.” Woodland Hills Indivisible had publicized the allegation on November 6, saying its community network had confirmed agents were staying there. A separate event listing advertised an “ICE OUT OF MARRIOTT” demonstration for Sunday evening, and here’s footage of the protest. This was posted on BlueSky, so naturally replies support a Marriott boycott, with one commenter listing out the brands because even Marriott execs can’t name them all. Another offers, “Projector resistance is an underappreciated art form.” And someone asks, “Motel 6 forget to leave the lights on?” I covered Motel 6 properties handing guest lists to ICE, and the chain’s subsequent $7.6 million settlement. Reporting your own guests to immigration authorities is a very different business strategy than renting rooms to the federal government. The Trump Hotel Got This Treatment, Too This immediately brings to mind the projections I wrote about at the former Trump International Hotel in Washington, D.C. in 2017. Artist Robin Bell projected “Emoluments Welcome” and “Pay Trump Bribes Here,” with an arrow pointing toward the entrance. He also displayed the Constitution’s emoluments clause. Projecting Light Isn’t Trespassing So can someone actually do this? In Wilson v. Interlake Steel, California’s Supreme Court said nondamaging intrusions of light, noise, or odor aren’t trespass. However, Light shining into occupied rooms would be nuisance if it’s sufficiently substantial and unreasonable. Actually putting the projection equipment on hotel property or blocking access could be actionable. And LA’s sign ordinance could be implicated – Los Angeles includes projected images in its sign definitions, with restrictions on supergraphic signs. I think it’s an interesting legal queston whether a temporary political display can be restricted based on a municipal sign ordinance but a neutral time, place and manner restriction seems plausible. Renting Rooms To Agents Isn’t The Same As Running A Detention Center The hotel is in HM Alpha Hotels & Resorts’ management portfolio. When HM Alpha announced taking over management, it identified the property as part of Southwest Value Partners’ portfolio. The hotel’s operator makes booking decisions, but a protest aimed at the Marriott name can spread the cost across the brand. Customers generally book a Marriott, not a particular real estate investment firm’s management arrangement. Still, renting an agent a room doesn’t establish that Marriott “loves Trump.” Back in 2019, Marriott, Hilton and Choice said they wouldn’t turn their hotels into immigration detention facilities. Marriott was also criticized for hosting a Customs and Border Protection trade symposium at the Marriott Marquis Chicago. I supported then-CEO Arne Sorenson’s argument that renting meeting space doesn’t mean endorsing a group’s views. Hotels shouldn’t need to agree with their guests’ politics before handing over a room key. I also covered Hilton telling properties to stop housing detained children, followed by government records showing children held at Hilton, Marriott and Choice properties. And Marriott’s neutrality claim looked awfully selective when a Prague hotel rejected a Uyghur conference. In January, Hilton removed a Minnesota Hampton Inn from its system after it continued refusing Homeland Security bookings. I’m not sure that refusing these bookings is something that the property would even be allowed to do, though post-midterms a lot of this is probably up in the air. And indeed the President himself has just walked back his own administration’s tough on immigration stance. (HT: Paul H) Topics on this pageProtestArne M. Spotted at Woodland Hills Marriott where ICE is reportedly staying.

— Raider (@iwillnotbesilenced.bsky.social) November 9, 2026

The messages include “Marriott houses the Gestapo,” “Marriott loves Trump” (with a heart), and “Marriott devours your tax dollars for fascism.” The closing message is: “We beat you before. We will beat you again.”

Woodland Hills Indivisible had publicized the allegation on November 6, saying its community network had confirmed agents were staying there. A separate event listing advertised an “ICE OUT OF MARRIOTT” demonstration for Sunday evening, and here’s footage of the protest.

This was posted on BlueSky, so naturally replies support a Marriott boycott, with one commenter listing out the brands because even Marriott execs can’t name them all. Another offers, “Projector resistance is an underappreciated art form.” And someone asks, “Motel 6 forget to leave the lights on?”

I covered Motel 6 properties handing guest lists to ICE, and the chain’s subsequent $7.6 million settlement. Reporting your own guests to immigration authorities is a very different business strategy than renting rooms to the federal government.

This immediately brings to mind the projections I wrote about at the former Trump International Hotel in Washington, D.C. in 2017. Artist Robin Bell projected “Emoluments Welcome” and “Pay Trump Bribes Here,” with an arrow pointing toward the entrance. He also displayed the Constitution’s emoluments clause. Projecting Light Isn’t Trespassing So can someone actually do this? In Wilson v. Interlake Steel, California’s Supreme Court said nondamaging intrusions of light, noise, or odor aren’t trespass. However, Light shining into occupied rooms would be nuisance if it’s sufficiently substantial and unreasonable. Actually putting the projection equipment on hotel property or blocking access could be actionable. And LA’s sign ordinance could be implicated – Los Angeles includes projected images in its sign definitions, with restrictions on supergraphic signs. I think it’s an interesting legal queston whether a temporary political display can be restricted based on a municipal sign ordinance but a neutral time, place and manner restriction seems plausible. Renting Rooms To Agents Isn’t The Same As Running A Detention Center The hotel is in HM Alpha Hotels & Resorts’ management portfolio. When HM Alpha announced taking over management, it identified the property as part of Southwest Value Partners’ portfolio. The hotel’s operator makes booking decisions, but a protest aimed at the Marriott name can spread the cost across the brand. Customers generally book a Marriott, not a particular real estate investment firm’s management arrangement. Still, renting an agent a room doesn’t establish that Marriott “loves Trump.” Back in 2019, Marriott, Hilton and Choice said they wouldn’t turn their hotels into immigration detention facilities. Marriott was also criticized for hosting a Customs and Border Protection trade symposium at the Marriott Marquis Chicago. I supported then-CEO Arne Sorenson’s argument that renting meeting space doesn’t mean endorsing a group’s views. Hotels shouldn’t need to agree with their guests’ politics before handing over a room key. I also covered Hilton telling properties to stop housing detained children, followed by government records showing children held at Hilton, Marriott and Choice properties. And Marriott’s neutrality claim looked awfully selective when a Prague hotel rejected a Uyghur conference. In January, Hilton removed a Minnesota Hampton Inn from its system after it continued refusing Homeland Security bookings. I’m not sure that refusing these bookings is something that the property would even be allowed to do, though post-midterms a lot of this is probably up in the air. And indeed the President himself has just walked back his own administration’s tough on immigration stance. (HT: Paul H) Topics on this pageProtestArne M. The hotel is in HM Alpha Hotels & Resorts’ management portfolio. When HM Alpha announced taking over management, it identified the property as part of Southwest Value Partners’ portfolio.

The hotel’s operator makes booking decisions, but a protest aimed at the Marriott name can spread the cost across the brand. Customers generally book a Marriott, not a particular real estate investment firm’s management arrangement. Still, renting an agent a room doesn’t establish that Marriott “loves Trump.”

Back in 2019, Marriott, Hilton and Choice said they wouldn’t turn their hotels into immigration detention facilities. Marriott was also criticized for hosting a Customs and Border Protection trade symposium at the Marriott Marquis Chicago.

I supported then-CEO Arne Sorenson’s argument that renting meeting space doesn’t mean endorsing a group’s views. Hotels shouldn’t need to agree with their guests’ politics before handing over a room key.

I also covered Hilton telling properties to stop housing detained children, followed by government records showing children held at Hilton, Marriott and Choice properties. And Marriott’s neutrality claim looked awfully selective when a Prague hotel rejected a Uyghur conference.

In January, Hilton removed a Minnesota Hampton Inn from its system after it continued refusing Homeland Security bookings. I’m not sure that refusing these bookings is something that the property would even be allowed to do, though post-midterms a lot of this is probably up in the air. And indeed the President himself has just walked back his own administration’s tough on immigration stance.

American Express Membership Rewards aren't just for travel anymore. Sports fans now have another way to put their points to use.

As of today, some American Express cardmembers can transfer Membership Rewards points to FanCash, the rewards currency of sports merchandise retailer Fanatics.

The new transfer option is part of a broader partnership between American Express and Fanatics, which also unveiled additional details about its upcoming cobranded credit card.

Eligible U.S. cardmembers can now transfer Membership Rewards points to FanCash at a rate of 1,000 points for $10 in FanCash, giving you a redemption value of 1 cent per point. You can find this option in the newly added Lifestyle section of Amex's transfer partners page.

Simply enter your Fanatics credentials to link your account, which only takes a few seconds.

Once transferred, FanCash can be used toward eligible purchases across the Fanatics ecosystem, including sports apparel, trading cards, collectibles and tickets.

However, this isn't necessarily the best use of your Amex points. At 1 cent apiece, you'd be getting just half of TPG's valuation of Membership Rewards points at 2 cents each, a value you can potentially achieve by transferring points to Amex's airline and hotel partners.

Still, this gives sports fans another option for redeeming their points, particularly if they don't have any upcoming travel plans.

Related: Best ways to use Amex Membership Rewards points

As announced earlier this year, American Express and Fanatics are also teaming up on a new cobranded credit card designed for sports fans.

The upcoming Fanatics American Express® Card will have no annual fee and earn 5% FanCash on eligible purchases across the Fanatics ecosystem, or 8% or more when shopping through the Fanatics app.

The card will also offer sports-focused perks and more than 500 trading card-inspired designs featuring professional athletes.

It's not yet available for applications, but interested consumers can join the waitlist.

The information for the Fanatics American Express Card has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

The ability to transfer Amex points to FanCash gives sports fans another way to use their rewards, but the 1-cent-per-point value may not appeal to travelers looking to maximize their Membership Rewards points.

For those who regularly shop with Fanatics, however, the new transfer option could be a convenient way to put unused points toward their next purchase.

Related: American Express Membership Rewards: How to earn, redeem and transfer points

#6215. How To Max Out Citi Strata Elite’s Impressive Credits

I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

I’ve been looking forward not just to spending a big initial bonus – now 75,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 in the first 3 months of account opening – but to making the most out of all of the credits that come with the Citi Strata EliteSM Card (See rates and fees.) As a new cardholder I dove into the specifics of the benefits. So here’s what to expect.

The Citi Strata EliteSM Card offers an annual $200 Splurge Credit. You receive up to $200 back on retailers including 1stDibs, American Airlines, Best Buy, Future Personal Training, and Live Nation. This benefit is on a calendar year basis. So during your first cardmember year you can actually claim it twice – once during the remainder of 2026, and again at the start of 2027. You can redeem it across one or more transactions. You don’t need to try to max it out in a single transaction – you won’t simply lose the remainder. In order to use the credit you first need to register for it and select up to two merchants at a time you’d like to use the credit for. The selection applies immediately (in fact, as of 12 a.m. Eastern time on the day you made the selection.) It may take up to to billing cycles to receive the credit. The credits can be used at two of 1stDibs; Live Nation; Best Buy; American Airlines; Future Personal Training. Bear in mind that some transactions won’t qualify – it’s based on the merchant of record: American Airlines or American Airlines Vacations needs to bill for the splurge credit to count. If you book related products and services with a different merchant of record (which even includes AAdvantage status renewal) those won’t count. Live Nation purchases need to be made at livenation.com or ticketmaster.com- – and for events held in the United States – third party fulfilled purchases won’t trigger the credit. The credit is super easy to use. I’ll just use the card for an American Airlines ticket. (This needs to be booked directly, not through Citi Travel or another travel portal.) Don’t have a booking right away and you’re about to hit end of year? Avoid basic economy fares, but buy a non-refundable ticket. If you cancel the ticket you’ll retain an American Airlines trip credit for future use. Or select Best Buy and make a purchase there. $100 Semi-Annual Blacklane Credit Blacklane sets up car services for you all over the world. It’s mostly pre-reserved. They’re in a lot more places than Uber and you’re getting a professional driver. At airports you’ll usually have them meet you at baggage claim and assist with luggage, for instance. And you’re going to get more consistently nice vehicles and better service than rideshare. They track your flight, arrive in advance and wait for you for an allowable time (like an hour). The card offers a $200 credit each year with Blacklane – $100 January – June and $100 July – December. No registration is required, just pay for Blacklane trips with the card and the statement credits trigger automatically. In London, Paris and Dubai I use Wheely. Most of the time in the U.S. I’ll use rideshare. But with my family, arriving after a couple of weeks abroad, I may want a car service pickup because the Austin airport makes you schlepp across the road and through a parking structure, changing levels, to reach rideshare pickup. Pre-arranged cars park by the terminal, and the driver is there to help with luggage. Pricing varies by airport and trip, but it’s often competitive with premium Uber services like BlackSUV. $300 Hotel Benefit Each year, Citi Strata Elite Card offers a $300 hotel credit for stays of two or more nights that are prepaid through Citi Travel. (Prepaid rates can still be cancellable and refundable.) The credit must be redeemed by the primary cardmember and is by calendar year (based on when you book, not the dates of your stay). A new cardmember could use the credit now and again at the start of 2027, so twice in their first cardmember year. $300 will be applied to your booking when you make the reservation – it’s not a statement credit that posts later. You can also use it across multiple transactions, e.g. if you had a 2-night stay that totaled only $200 you’d still have $100 to use later. While the card earns 12x on hotels you use it to pay for with Citi Travel, you don’t earn points on the charges covered by this credit. Consider these OTA bookings. Pricing can vary and you’re often getting the same rate as elsewhere – but not discounted rates like AAA, or member rates. You also aren’t usually entitled to hotel loyalty points, elite stay credit, or elite benefits. Priority Pass The card offers a Priority Pass Select membership for the primary cardmember and any authorized users (which are $75 each), valid for unlimited visits and including up to two complimentary guests.. It does not cover credits at restaurants and similar non-lounge offerings like markets that are linked to Priority Pass. You don’t need to have your physical or even digital Priority Pass membership for access – rather uniquely lounges are supposed to accept your Strata Elite card as the Priority Pass card itself. That means, unlike other issuers, you don’t have to activate Priority Pass membership. Marco Polo Lounge, Venice Admirals Club Passes The card comes with 4 Admirals Club passes per calendar year (so twice in cardmember year one, for eight passes total). Each set of four has to be used during the calendar year in which they’re issued, and expire if unused. They are available to the primary cardmember and include one guest 18 years or older plus up to 3 children under 18. They can be redeemed for additional adult companions as well. Requires same day boarding pass (departing or arriving) for an American or oneworld partner airline flight. Valid for 24 hours, and can be used at multiple lounges on the same day. The passes are deposited to your AAdvanage wallet and can be scanned by the Admirals Club front desk for entry. Upon card account closure, unused passes are forfeit. Admirals Club Washington National Airport E Concourse Applying For This Card Was An Easy Decision Citi’s new premium card is pretty incredible in the first year, not just because of the strong initial bonus but also because of credits that are timed to calendar year rather than cardmember year. (Calendar year credits can be claimed twice in cardmember year one.) Honestly, I feel like this was a strategic error on Citi’s part. They’ve constructed a card that is a no-brainer to get. There’s just so much value to the customer up front. I’m not sure if it’ll be a keeper long-term or a card that’s best for your everyday spend (although it is very good). My take: apply for this card, reap the maximum benefits in year one, and then consider whether it’s right for you in the long-term. #6214. Highest To Lowest: How To Get From JFK To Manhattan For Just $3

In the film Highest 2 Lowest (2025), starring Denzel Washington, legendary filmmaker Spike Lee portrays two distinct sides of New York City, depending on your altitude and bank account. Nowhere is that contrast more apparent than in the choices travelers face when commuting between Manhattan and John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK).

Whether you are a visiting traveler or an NYC resident, navigating to and from the city’s primary international hub is a perpetual balancing act between cost, comfort, and time. Previously, I detailed what is literally and figuratively the “highest” mode of airport transit: Blade’s helicopter transfers (starting at $195 and easily topping $300, though rides can cost you nothing out of pocket using Bilt Cash). Each Bilt Cash award expires 12 months after you earn it, on the last day of that month.

In this Reader Story, I’m taking you down, subterranean, to the lowest option available: the Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s (MTA) $3 bus-to-subway hack.

Duke Ellington was onto something: “Take the ‘A’ Train.” However, he didn’t specify which A train branch, nor did he mention that a quick bus transfer might be involved!

Even some locals may ask: “Wait, isn’t the AirTrain $8.75, plus a $3 subway fare?” That’s true if you exit the AirTrain at Jamaica or Howard Beach. However, there is a lesser-known and dramatically cheaper workaround: just $3 total from JFK to nearly anywhere in NYC with the MTA, provided you don’t mind adding a few extra minutes to your journey.

For the reverse trip, take any Lefferts Blvd-bound A train, ensuring the destination sign explicitly says “Lefferts Blvd” rather than Far Rockaway or Rockaway Park. Importantly, Far Rockaway A trains often display “JFK Airport” on their digital side displays because most travelers use the more expensive $8.75 Howard Beach transfer route, so do not board those if you want the $3-only route. Once on the correct train, get off at Liberty Ave / Lefferts Blvd, exit to the street, locate the bus stop, catch a JFK-bound Q10 or Q80 bus to the Lefferts AirTrain station, and take the free AirTrain directly to your terminal.

If you type “JFK Airport” into Google Maps or Apple Maps, the app will almost never display the $3-only hack. Navigation algorithms prioritize minimizing the number of transit transfers over saving money, automatically suppressing the bus transfer in favor of the standard $8.75 AirTrain connection at Jamaica or Howard Beach.

Even typing “Lefferts Blvd AirTrain Station” into navigation apps often causes confusion because the AirTrain station and the Ozone Park A-train terminal are located roughly 1.5 miles apart.

To force your map app to show the correct route, search for the street-level bus-to-subway transfer point at “Lefferts Blvd & Liberty Ave.” From JFK, this will display the Q10 Rush or Q80 bus taking you to the A train turnstiles; from Manhattan, it will guide you on the Lefferts-bound A train directly to your bus connection.

Other than extreme weather events, strikes, and major crises, all three legs of this route—the AirTrain, the Q10/Q80 bus, and the A Train—operate 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, though timing varies. During daytime and peak hours (6:00 AM – 10:00 PM), AirTrain cars run every 7–10 minutes, Q10 and Q80 buses depart roughly every 8–15 minutes, and A trains run frequently as express services through Brooklyn and Manhattan.

However, late-night transit frequency changes significantly in NYC, so keep that in mind for overnight or early-morning flights: AirTrain headways drop to 15–20 minute intervals, late-night Q10/Q80 bus departures stretch to every 20–30 minutes, and the A train may shift to local-only service (check MTA Service Status for possible re-routings).

Thanks to the flat-fare structure of the New York City Subway (as opposed to distance-based transit networks found in cities like London, Tokyo, or Washington, D.C.), that single $3 fare (and free transfer) unlocks access to nearly the entire city once you pass through the turnstiles at the Ozone Park–Lefferts Boulevard station.

Because there are no exit turnstiles or zone caps inside the subway network, you can ride from Queens through Brooklyn, up Manhattan, and deep into the Bronx, all on that same initial $3 tap—as long as you stay within the fare-paid zone. And, if you exit the subway system in Lower Manhattan, you can walk over to Whitehall Terminal and board the free Staten Island Ferry to reach the fifth and final borough. While attempting to tap onto a Staten Island bus or the Staten Island Railway (SIR) on the other side would consume a second $3 fare (and likely break the 2-hour transfer clock), at least JFK to Manhattan for $3 remains one of the greatest transit bargains in the world.

All told—AirTrain, bus, and subway—you can get between JFK and Manhattan in about 75 to 90 minutes. Depending on brutal rush-hour highway traffic, you might even tie or beat a $100+ rideshare. That said, I would recommend this route exclusively for those traveling light (backpacks and carry-ons), willing to spend the extra time, and comfortable navigating city transit. But for the right traveler, it is a relatively safe, clean, reliable, and wildly affordable hack.

To put the $3 bus-to-subway hack into perspective, it helps to see how it stacks up against the other primary options for traveling between Manhattan and JFK:

Of course, there are other, less conventional ways of getting to and from JFK:

Whether taking a $300+ helicopter ride or a $3 bus-to-subway hack, commuting between JFK and Manhattan truly captures the two contrasting sides of New York City that Spike Lee brings to life in Highest 2 Lowest.

For light packers on a budget, the Lefferts Boulevard Q10 transfer stands as the undefeated champion of pure value. Duke Ellington was right all along—if you want to get to Sugar Hill or anywhere else in the city without breaking the bank, simply take the “A” train!

With so many options available, what’s your preferred way of getting to or from JFK, and which are your preferred payment methods to maximize value?

These are great hacks for people who know what they are doing. Not being from New York, I'd prefer a bus or shuttle. These train/bus methods seem to have too many possibilities for errors and confusion for a first-timer on their own. The old Airporter buses suited my needs just fine. As a general proposition, I think airport buses are the best airport-to-central-city option for people with anything more than a backpack who are unfamiliar with the local transportation system. When I don't know the train system, I worry about missing a stop, and crowds make everything worse even if only traveling with a carry-on and backpack. A bus solves those problems and lets me enjoy the views in a new city. Usually the bus gets me to the destination or close enough to walk or enjoy (usually) a short taxi ride.

I have done this several times lefferts to A teainat Ozone Park (Brooklyn and Lower Manhattan)and leffers to E train (Long Island City and Mid-town Manhattan) depending on where I am going. I either stay in hotels in Downtown Brooklyn or Long Island City as they are at least $150 cheaper/night when you factor amenity fees in Manhattan Hotels. Extra travel time via Lefferts is 30-40 mins. BTW, the A train MTA Ozone Park station is in the middle of Little Guyana. Best damn double double roti and curry for $10

Great write up! Also wanted to add that they finally re-did the AirTrain discount fares after switching to the OMNY card. IF you always tap with the same credit card (or apple pay, etc) you have a 30-day rolling fee cap of $43.50 (aka 5 rides). There's also a group discount, so if you tap the same payment method repeatedly in a 5 minute window, each of the riders after you are discounted to $4.50 (up to 4 guests).

Nice writeup! On a similar note, in Vienna you can skip the (relatively) expensive CAT (city airport train) and take the RailJet RJ, REX, or S-Bahn line S7 to the city for less than a third of the price (4.60 or so vs 14.90, and it's faster too). The trains also may get you closer to where you actually need to go (e.g. the main train station) rather than Wien Mitte only for the CAT. Note thought that there is some construction affecting the REX and S7 lines for the next year so you either have to catch a RJ to the main station or get off the S7/REX at St. Marx and take the tram or bus from there until the work is completed.

#6213. 3,700 Miles: TAP Air Portugal Unveils New Unusual Longest A321LR Route

TAP Air Portugal is planning a significant change to its Porto–Luanda service, deploying the Airbus A321LR on the 3,737-mile (6,014 km) route from October 31, 2027. The move will create the airline's longest scheduled nonstop A321LR flight, narrowly surpassing its existing Lisbon–Belém service.

The decision is particularly noteworthy because TAP intends to replace its 298-seat Airbus A330-900 with a 171-seat narrowbody, reducing passenger capacity by approximately 43%. The long sector also raises questions about baggage and payload limitations, particularly given the substantial baggage requirements that can characterize routes between Europe and sub-Saharan Africa. The change remains provisional, with almost a year until its planned introduction.

According to AeroRoutes, TAP's preliminary winter 2027/28 schedule replaces the A330-900 with the A321LR on its twice-weekly service from Porto to Luanda. The route connects northern Portugal with Angola's new Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport, which has progressively replaced the city's older airport. The proposed flight schedule is detailed below.

The aircraft substitution will reduce weekly capacity from 1,192 to 684 seats across both directions, a reduction of 508 seats. TAP's A321LR configuration accommodates 16 business-class passengers and 155 economy passengers, compared with 34 business and 264 economy seats on its A330-900s. The smaller aircraft could allow TAP to better match capacity with demand while maintaining nonstop service. When TAP first received the A321LR, then-CEO Antonoaldo Neves explained its strategic importance:

“With its superior range, we can comfortably explore new markets in North America, South America and Africa from Portugal, and offer nonstop flights with the right size of aircraft.”

However, the long flight raises operational questions. Airbus advertises an A321LR range of approximately 4,000 nautical miles, equivalent to 4,603 miles (7,408 km), comfortably exceeding Porto–Luanda's great-circle distance of 3,737 miles (6,014 km) on paper. Nevertheless, the aircraft's range depends on payload and operating conditions.

Heavy checked baggage, commercial cargo, headwinds, and fuel reserves could all influence its performance. TAP has not announced any passenger or baggage restrictions, and whether either will be necessary remains unknown.

The Porto–Luanda deployment will surpass TAP's Lisbon–Belém service by just 11 miles (18 km). The Portuguese flag carrier has increasingly used its A321LRs to connect smaller long-haul markets across the Atlantic, particularly in northeastern Brazil and North America.

Its introduction of the aircraft transformed TAP's transatlantic network, allowing the airline to serve destinations previously impossible to operate economically because they would have required larger widebodies to cover the distance. TAP's planned 2027 A321LR network includes 16 nonstop routes exceeding 2,000 miles (3,219 km).

Six of the ten longest connect Portugal with the Americas, three serve Brazil specifically, and the new Porto–Luanda service is the only African route on the list. The ranking illustrates the versatility of an aircraft that TAP originally introduced to complement its A330-900 fleet. Crucially, the record applies only to nonstop flights: TAP has operated longer one-stop A321LR services, including Lisbon–Belém–Manaus, covering a combined 4,534 miles (7,297 km).

Introduced in November 2024, the three-weekly service was scheduled to take 11 hours and 45 minutes, including its stop in Belém. TAP has also just launched a triangular Lisbon–São Luís–Fortaleza–Lisbon service, demonstrating how intermediate stops extend the reach of its long-haul narrowbody fleet.

Simple Flying had the chance to check out this narrowbody flying over the Atlantic!

The destination is itself undergoing a major transformation. Dr. António Agostinho Neto International Airport (NBJ) was inaugurated in November 2023, approximately 25 miles (40 km) south-east of central Luanda, replacing Quatro de Fevereiro Airport (LAD) as the city's principal passenger gateway.

Angola's national carrier, TAAG Angola Airlines, transferred its international operations in October 2025, while the wider transition was completed in March 2026. The airport forms part of Angola's ambition to establish a major Southern African aviation hub. The approximately $3 billion facility is designed to handle 15 million passengers annually, supported by two runways and substantial cargo infrastructure.

TAAG Angola Airlines, TAP, Air France, Lufthansa, Ethiopian, Qatar Airways, Royal Air Maroc, Airlink

However, its initial traffic has been considerably lower than anticipated. Just over 750,000 passengers used the airport during 2025, although that figure reflects a transitional year before all scheduled airlines had relocated. Despite its ambitious scale, the airport faces challenges attracting and retaining international services.

Turkish Airlines removed Luanda from its network in 2026, following the withdrawal of Brussels Airlines last year. Nevertheless, TAP, Lufthansa, Air France, and several African carriers maintain connections. TAP's planned A321LR substitution illustrates how it is able to adjust capacity to demand and still maintain the nonstop service.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#6212. Passenger Takes Another Man’s Aisle Seat To Sit With His Wife—Frontier Flight Attendant Lets Him Keep It

A Frontier Airlines passenger found another man in his assigned aisle seat. The man wanted to sit beside his wife, so he offered the passenger his middle seat two rows back. A flight attendant listened to a passenger’s plea to sit in his assigned seat but did nothing. The passenger finally gave up: “I just want to get home.” The seat stealer on flight 1550 from Atlanta to Jacksonville on Sunday got what he wanted. And the airline – which sells these seat assignments – left them to negotiate amongst themselves, creating a secondary market. The flight was full, a long-haired man in his 20s arrived at seat 28C, and a white-haired man in his 60s was already sitting there beside his wife. When the younger passenger pointed out that this was his assigned seat, the response was: “Well, I wanted to sit next to my wife. You can have my middle seat (30E).” The younger man waited. A flight attendant got involved and heard the story, the witness says. After nothing happened, he walked back to 30E and sat down. Several commenters say the displaced passenger should have insisted on his assignment or asked a second crewmember for help. Some suggest flight attendants shouldn’t get involved because unlike at Delta, American and United their pay at Frontier isn’t calculating including boarding time. Some think the best solution would be to stand in the aisle, refuse to move, and demand compensation. A couple can ask for a seat swap. They can offer money. They can ask a flight attendant for help finding two willing passengers. But stealing someone’s seat isn’t acceptable. Still, sometimes it’s permitted. I covered an American Airlines passenger whose paid aisle seat was occupied by a child. He said a flight attendant backed the family because “She got on the plane before you,” called him “the bad guy,” and threatened to remove him. It seems to me that at a minimum the passenger here is owed a refund for his seat fee. There’s no involuntary denied boarding. There’s no downgrade of class of service. So anything more than that is discretionary customer service on the part of the airline. Morally the passenger is owed more. I’d surely ask for another crewmember’s involvement if I got nowhere with the first flight attendant. Unfortunately, in the moment, it doesn’t matter whether the passenger is right or wrong. They’re at the mercy of what the crew says, even when the crewmember just shrugs. All you have to do is not sit down and they will fix it.

Yeah, it’s a one hour flight. Live to fight another day. But if he paid for that aisle seat assignment, then he’s owed at least that amount.

Hilarious when a working girl is labeled by her customer as his “wife.”

“Oh, I wanted to to sit in First Class. You can have my center seat in Row 99.” Don’t tell me that’s not coming one of these days.

And this is a good reason why one shouldn’t fly Frontier.

I’m sorry, I know FAs are there ‘for your safety’ but let’s be clear their job is much more than that. Forget the middle vs. aisle debate, if carriers are going to charge for seat assignments, especially when they charge more for certain seats (ie aisles) than others (ie middles), then they need to enforce the assignments. Seat assignments are not guaranteed, even when one pays – I realize that – though airlines if they move you will at least refund. This FA needs, at a minimum, re-training.

Frontier should refund the guy who paid for the aisle seat, plus at least a portion of the airfare for this segment. Seat stealer guy should have the card that was used to buy the ticket charged for the seat, and not allowed to fly Frontier without paying for a seat assignment first (or should just be auto-assigned the middle seat in the last row of the aircraft forever). Once people try this and think they can get away with it, they will try again and again. They get what they want without the financial cost that those of us who abide by the rules need to pay.

And while this could theoretically happen on any airline, in my experience, it doesn’t because the FAs seem to take authority on the seating issues on the major carriers. Sometimes, they will actively look for solutions (so a parent can sit next to their child, etc.).

Add to the long list of reasons NOT to fly Frontier…

Additonally. The whole idea of confirmed seats becomes moot if this kind of flight attendant error is allowed to recur.

And why stop within classes of service? If a seat is free in first, why cannot someone in a middle seat in coach take it with just a perfunctory excuse “I have long legs”, “I have a family history of DVT”, “my hamster died of DVT”, etc?

The result is not the frontier, it is anarchy.

If somebody had wanted my seat they should have paid to select it. There’s no way I would hand over my chosen seat to some cheap sleazebag who thought they could just take what they want. I would die on that hill.

I too prefer the aisle seat and pay accordingly. If it had been me, I would have played the “grandpa” card. Even though I have all my hair and teeth, I also have an enlarged prostate. If the FA doesn’t mind me dribbling on the other passengers, I suggest you let me keep that aisle seat.

Separated couples who are desperate to sit together will happen more often in business class with business lite fares that only allow seat assignments 24 hours before departure. At that point, there’s almost never two empty seats together or even across from each other. And the couple having an equal or better seat to trade is problematic. Hopefully, a desperate partner won’t just plop down in the desired seat, but the partner may feel justified. Argument ensues. This is another reason for getting to your assigned seat asap.

I just wonder why it is always a middle seat that gets exchanged for a better located seat? why do they never ask another aisle seat passenger to change to an equal location (or arguably a better location because it is closer to the exit) seat and keep their assigned/ given to them middle seat? that would be reasonable and acceptable solution, but all these stories are about someone pirating a better seat under pretense that they want to seat together. The fact that the flight attendant did not intervene is unacceptable

This is the sort of thing when you hire a flying waitress.

Why does a flight attendant do that? It is easier for them. I had something similar happen once and the flight attendant told me the reason she was letting the old man get away with it was that I was the nicer person to deal with.

For the first time I recall I actually asked another passenger if they would swap seats so I could sit next to my grown daughter. (We’d switched flights the day of.) But in my defense, I began by saying “feel free to say no”, and it was BA F on a daytime international flight, so all seats are pretty good. I have agreed to switch to allow a couple to sit together in international business class before, but it was on a flight where all seats had aisle access, so didn’t really care.

FFS. The guy couldn’t be separated from his wife for an hour? Should have bought 2 seats together. I would not have yielded so easily.

The steward/ess’s behaviour was despicable.

Airbnb disclosed in its quarterly SEC filing that it sold intellectual property to a private AI lab founded and controlled by CEO Brian Chesky, with CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle holding a stake and both executives working for the entity. The November transaction brought Airbnb $7.1 million in cash covering the IP and expense reimbursements combined, and a special committee of independent, disinterested directors approved it under the company's related-party transaction policy. In return, Airbnb received a license to certain lab IP for internal use and the right to invest in future equity rounds, though the filing does not identify the IP, explain its valuation, separate the purchase price from expenses, or disclose the license economics. Airbnb said the executives' roles at the lab will not change their responsibilities to the company. The arrangement lands as Airbnb prepares a proprietary AI travel agent for the first half of 2027, built to assemble maps, photos, comparisons, calendars, and itineraries around guest queries. Neither the filing nor the shareholder update says whether that agent draws on the lab's technology, or whether the lab could license the same IP to competitors such as Booking Holdings or Expedia.

The American Express® Gold Card is one of Amex’s most compelling cards for earning Membership Rewards points, and it currently has a best-ever welcome offer that’s as high as 100,000 bonus points, making it a great time to apply. In this post, I’d like to go over all the details of the current Amex Gold Card bonus, including who is eligible, and why you might want to apply.

Link: Learn more about the American Express® Gold Card

The Amex Gold Card currently has a lucrative bonus, marketed as being as high as 100,000 Membership Rewards bonus points after spending $8,000 within the first six months. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer.

The way this works, you can apply for the Amex Gold Card, and then find out your offer amount. Then you can decide whether you want to accept the offer or not. That’s an unconventional approach for a welcome offer. At least Amex has the “apply with confidence” feature, so there won’t be a hard pull unless you accept the offer.

Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Membership Rewards points to be worth 1.7 cents each. As a point of comparison, previously the Amex Gold Card bonus offered up to 60,000 points, so this is a lot better. As a matter of fact, the current Amex Gold Card offer is potentially the best publicly available one that we’ve seen.

There are lots of great uses for Amex points, as they can be transferred to roughly 20 airline and hotel partners, ranging from Air Canada Aeroplan, to Air France-KLM Flying Blue, All Nippon Airways Mileage Club, to Virgin Atlantic Flying Club. Just to give a couple of quick examples:

This is a reason to pick up the Amex Gold Card before you pick up the Amex Platinum Card. That’s because you’re potentially eligible for the Amex Platinum Card welcome offer if you have or have had the Amex Gold Card, while the inverse may not be true.

On top of that, Amex’s general card restrictions apply. There are a couple of additional things to note:

For one, it’s an amazing card in terms of the return on spending, especially for anyone who loves to eat (and who doesn’t?). The card offers the following Membership Rewards points multipliers for spending:

On top of that, the Amex Gold Card offers up to $424 in credits annually, which can help recoup much of the annual fee (or more than offset the annual fee, in some cases). These credits are with Uber, Resy, Dunkin’, and more, and are summarized in the below chart (Enrollment is required for select benefits).

The Amex Gold Card also offers Hertz Five Star status just for having the card (enrollment required), which can get you valuable perks.

Essentially, if you spend a lot on food (whether at restaurants or supermarkets) and if you can get some value out of the credits, I tend to think the Amex Gold Card is easy to justify.

#6209. Uber Wants You To Drive Yourself—Reserve Parking In 15 Cities, Earn 10% Back

Uber is launching parking reservations in 15 U.S. cities, letting you find a garage or lot, compare prices, and pay inside its app. Uber One members earn 10% back in credits on eligible bookings and of course Uber One comes with Amex Platinum. It’s a little weird to have self-service Uber. You supply the car. You do the driving. But they offer Uber Eats for pickup, so I guess? Still, even if it’s not gig workers and urban mobility, if the price and rebate are good, ok then. Where Uber Parking Is Available Uber’s November 9 launch covers Atlanta, Austin, Boston, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, Nashville, New York City, Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington, D.C. They plan to expand across the United States. This follows Uber’s acquisition of SpotHero, announced in February. SpotHero’s broader network has more than 13,000 garages, lots, and valet locations across over 400 cities in the U.S. and Canada. However, Uber’s parking page lists 7,000 facilities. Tap Parking in the Uber app, enter your destination and parking times, and compare the map’s prices. You can filter for self-parking or valet, garages or surface lots, and things like on-site staff. Enter your vehicle details and license plate, pay via your Uber Wallet, and follow the entry instructions on the parking pass. Uber already has your account and payment information. SpotHero had parking reservations. Now it’s in one place with Uber rebates. 10% Rebate, Including Taxes And Fees Uber One members earn 10% credits on eligible completed parking reservations including the parking charge, taxes, and fees. Credits generally arrive within 24 hours after the reservation. Not every location or reservation qualifies. Uber One costs $9.99 a month or $96 a year. Buying an annual membership solely for parking requires $960 in eligible annual parking purchases just to earn $96 in credits, assuming you use those credits at full value. So this is for someone who already has Uber One. Can You Use Amex Uber Cash? And Does Amazon Help? Uber Cash works at supported parking locations. Uber’s parking help page says so, and Uber’s American Express terms say: The Amex Benefit may be applied to any services to which Uber permits Uber Cash to be applied. So this is a new way to use monthly Uber credits ($15 monthly, plus another $20 in December). Consumer Gold offers $10 monthly. And you can get Uber One via Amex Platinum: up to $120 in statement credits per calendar year for membership fees charged directly to the card. Both monthly and annual plans qualify. (Consumer Centurion cards have a membership credit as well.) Keep Uber Cash off for the membership payment so Amex is charged and can reimburse it. Amazon Prime doesn’t unlock this. The new U.S. Amazon arrangement provides $0 delivery fees on eligible Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more placed through Amazon, but doesn’t give you an Uber One membership. Those orders use a separate account and Uber One benefits don’t apply to them. Uber Isn’t The Only Option In This Market There are plenty of alternatives. Alternative   What To Compare SpotHero directly   The same underlying parking business, with a broader geographic footprint and hourly, monthly, event, and airport parking. ParkWhiz and BestParking   Other booking channels for prepaid garage and lot reservations, including event parking. ParkMobile and PayByPhone   Useful for paying for and extending parking in participating locations. ParkMobile also offers advance reservations. AirportParkingReservations.com and Way.com   Airport parking comparisons, including off-airport lots and hotel parking. Compare shuttle schedules, operating hours, and cancellation rules. The garage, hotel, event venue, or airport directly   Prepaid offers, parking packages, validation, and loyalty discounts that might beat an intermediary’s price. I’ve written about the economics of empty parking spaces: the garage already exists, and an unsold hour is revenue the operator never gets back. Advance booking can give operators a way to discount to people who compare prices while charging more to drivers who just show up. Uber says many participating locations offer rates below their drive-up prices. Read The Parking Pass Before You Pay Uber’s parking rules leave several decisions to the individual facility: Cancellation. Uber says most options can be canceled free before the start time, but the deadline shown for your reservation controls. Extensions. Most active reservations can be extended if space is available but don’t assume you can stay indefinitely at the original rate. Entry and exit. Follow the pass’s barcode, license plate, or attendant instructions. Most participating facilities don’t allow repeated entry and exit during one reservation. Vehicle restrictions and extra charges. Check height limits and oversized vehicle charges, along with early entry and late exit rules. Uber’s charge guidance flags additional fees. A reservation doesn’t imply a particular space is being held. SpotHero says it manages inventory with operators rather than physically holding a specific stall. If you arrive and can’t enter or the lot is full, Uber directs you to the parking pass’s help option. Good luck. There are two other launch limitations in Uber’s FAQ: business profiles aren’t supported, and Uber and SpotHero accounts can’t be linked. An Uber reservation won’t appear in your SpotHero account. The claim in the launch pitch that Americans spend an average of 17 hours a year looking for parking comes from a July 2017 study. It seems to me there’s very high variance in this. In fact, isn’t one solution just to Uber? Uber gets a transaction from people who choose to drive, then offers credits that encourage them to come back for a ride or food order. They also say they’ll explore using parking locations to stage autonomous vehicles between trips. They’re going to be losing their Waymo partnership so I wonder what that looks like? What I’d Really Like Is Uber Valet About a decade ago, Luxe offered a valet would meet you at your destination, take your car away to park it, and bring it back when you were ready. Zirx did, too. Walking into a restaurant while somebody dealt with your car was super value add! But it’s a tough business. Luxe ended its consumer valet service in 2017, and Volvo bought its technology, team, and other assets that September. Zirx stopped consumer valet service in February 2016. Attendants had to reach customers, park their cars, and return them, on top of paying for parking and insurance. Uber considered buying Luxe’s assets and engineers before Volvo did. Valet Network in New York advertises $10 parking, using street spaces. Apparently the service is in Carroll Gardens, Cobble Hill, and the Lower East Side and it’s another $3 to return the car. Ector offers something like this at French airports and train stations. That seems like an Uber feature, this is more like selling hotels through the app because they already have customers and their customers travel. I liked the old Travis vision for the company so much better. They had some growing up to do and maybe they wouldn’t have achieved everything before the VC cash ran out but this just isn’t that exciting of a vision, even if you have something new to do with existing Uber credits. So this is for someone who already has Uber One. Can You Use Amex Uber Cash? And Does Amazon Help? Uber Cash works at supported parking locations. Uber’s parking help page says so, and Uber’s American Express terms say: The Amex Benefit may be applied to any services to which Uber permits Uber Cash to be applied. So this is a new way to use monthly Uber credits ($15 monthly, plus another $20 in December). Consumer Gold offers $10 monthly. And you can get Uber One via Amex Platinum: up to $120 in statement credits per calendar year for membership fees charged directly to the card. Both monthly and annual plans qualify. (Consumer Centurion cards have a membership credit as well.) Keep Uber Cash off for the membership payment so Amex is charged and can reimburse it. Amazon Prime doesn’t unlock this. The new U.S. Amazon arrangement provides $0 delivery fees on eligible Uber Eats restaurant orders of $25 or more placed through Amazon, but doesn’t give you an Uber One membership. Those orders use a separate account and Uber One benefits don’t apply to them. Uber Isn’t The Only Option In This Market There are plenty of alternatives. Alternative   What To Compare SpotHero directly   The same underlying parking business, with a broader geographic footprint and hourly, monthly, event, and airport parking. ParkWhiz and BestParking   Other booking channels for prepaid garage and lot reservations, including event parking. ParkMobile and PayByPhone   Useful for paying for and extending parking in participating locations. ParkMobile also offers advance reservations. AirportParkingReservations.com and Way.com   Airport parking comparisons, including off-airport lots and hotel parking. Compare shuttle schedules, operating hours, and cancellation rules. The garage, hotel, event venue, or airport directly   Prepaid offers, parking packages, validation, and loyalty discounts that might beat an intermediary’s price. I’ve written about the economics of empty parking spaces: the garage already exists, and an unsold hour is revenue the operator never gets back. Advance booking can give operators a way to discount to people who compare prices while charging more to drivers who just show up. Uber says many participating locations offer rates below their drive-up prices. Read The Parking Pass Before You Pay Uber’s parking rules leave several decisions to the individual facility: Cancellation. Uber says most options can be canceled free before the start time, but the deadline shown for your reservation controls. Extensions. Most active reservations can be extended if space is available but don’t assume you can stay indefinitely at the original rate. Entry and exit. Follow the pass’s barcode, license plate, or attendant instructions. Most participating facilities don’t allow repeated entry and exit during one reservation. Vehicle restrictions and extra charges. Check height limits and oversized vehicle charges, along with early entry and late exit rules. Uber’s charge guidance flags additional fees. A reservation doesn’t imply a particular space is being held. SpotHero says it manages inventory with operators rather than physically holding a specific stall. If you arrive and can’t enter or the lot is full, Uber directs you to the parking pass’s help option. Good luck. There are two other launch limitations in Uber’s FAQ: business profiles aren’t supported, and Uber and SpotHero accounts can’t be linked. An Uber reservation won’t appear in your SpotHero account. The claim in the launch pitch that Americans spend an average of 17 hours a year looking for parking comes from a July 2017 study. It seems to me there’s very high variance in this. In fact, isn’t one solution just to Uber? Uber gets a transaction from people who choose to drive, then offers credits that encourage them to come back for a ride or food order. They also say they’ll explore using parking locations to stage autonomous vehicles between trips. They’re going to be losing their Waymo partnership so I wonder what that looks like? What I’d Really Like Is Uber Valet About a decade ago, Luxe offered a valet would meet you at your destination, take your car away to park it, and bring it back when you were ready. Zirx did, too. Walking into a restaurant while somebody dealt with your car was super value add! But it’s a tough business. Luxe ended its consumer valet service in 2017, and Volvo bought its technology, team, and other assets that September. Zirx stopped consumer valet service in February 2016. Attendants had to reach customers, park their cars, and return them, on top of paying for parking and insurance. Uber considered buying Luxe’s assets and engineers before Volvo did. Valet Network in New York advertises $10 parking, using street spaces. Apparently the service is in Carroll Gardens, Cobble Hill, and the Lower East Side and it’s another $3 to return the car. Ector offers something like this at French airports and train stations. That seems like an Uber feature, this is more like selling hotels through the app because they already have customers and their customers travel. I liked the old Travis vision for the company so much better. They had some growing up to do and maybe they wouldn’t have achieved everything before the VC cash ran out but this just isn’t that exciting of a vision, even if you have something new to do with existing Uber credits. Uber’s November 9 launch covers Atlanta, Austin, Boston, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, Nashville, New York City, Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington, D.C. They plan to expand across the United States.

This follows Uber’s acquisition of SpotHero, announced in February. SpotHero’s broader network has more than 13,000 garages, lots, and valet locations across over 400 cities in the U.S. and Canada. However, Uber’s parking page lists 7,000 facilities.

Tap Parking in the Uber app, enter your destination and parking times, and compare the map’s prices. You can filter for self-parking or valet, garages or surface lots, and things like on-site staff. Enter your vehicle details and license plate, pay via your Uber Wallet, and follow the entry instructions on the parking pass.

Uber already has your account and payment information. SpotHero had parking reservations. Now it’s in one place with Uber rebates.

#6208. Aviation’s Next Disaster Could Be In Your Carry-On

Enter your email for a complimentary article + exclusive offers.

Battery incidents are rising and airlines are tightening restrictions, with cabin crews the last line of defense. Is the industry doing enough to prevent the next fire, or simply getting better at putting them out?

The culprit was small enough to fit in a pocket, but the consequences were big enough to turn a Boeing 777 around over the Atlantic.

On September 17, a portable charger caught fire aboard KLM flight 735 from Amsterdam to Curaçao. The crew extinguished the flames and the jet returned safely to the Dutch capital. One person was injured and the incident led to knock-on cancellations, overnight accommodation for hundreds of passengers, and the plane being out of service until September 20.

An intriguing twist soon followed when Dutch media reported that the device allegedly belonged to Camiel Eurlings, KLM's former chief executive. The airline has declined to identify the passenger and Eurlings did not respond to Skift’s request for comment. On November 4, the Dutch Safety Board opened an independent investigation into the incident.

The reported CEO connection attracted international tabloid attention, but the passenger's identity is secondary to a broa

Tags: air safety, airlines, jet stream, skift feature

Skift provides the insights. You make the decisions.

Decision intelligence for travel leaders.

A portable charger fire aboard KLM flight 735 from Amsterdam to Curaçao on September 17 forced the Boeing 777 to turn back, injured one person, triggered cancellations, and kept the aircraft out of service until September 20. Dutch media reported the device allegedly belonged to former KLM CEO Camiel Eurlings; the airline declined to identify the passenger, and the Dutch Safety Board opened an investigation on November 4. The incident sits inside a sharply worsening trend. The UK Civil Aviation Authority estimates the average passenger now carries four lithium-powered devices, and its reports of passenger devices overheating rose 98% between 2024 and 2025. The FAA logged 97 lithium-battery incidents involving smoke, fire, or extreme heat in 2025, against 47 in 2017, and deputy director Paul Serafin said the agency has recently seen roughly two incidents a week on passenger aircraft. UL Standards & Engagement estimates an average cost of about $96,000 per event, with about 12% of incidents in its dataset resulting in a diversion or emergency landing. New ICAO provisions that took effect at the end of March cap passengers at two power banks and prohibit recharging them in flight, but implementation varies by jurisdiction and airlines can set stricter limits. Battery safety expert Paul Christensen said the airline industry needs to wake up as a matter of extreme urgency; IATA's Jonathan Jasper cautioned that most reports involve overheating rather than full thermal runaway.
